RE: 400 East Main Street, Cabot, Ar, 72023
Dear Keith Caldwell,

On 2/17/2022 the aforementioned property address was inspected and found standing in non-
compliance with the City of Cabot Nuisance Abatement Code and/or City of Cabot Unified
Development Code. You are receiving this letter due to inspections of the premises and you
(being listed as the owner of the property) must bring said property into compliance with the City
of Cabot's Code of Ordinances. All structures on said property of dilapidated condition (both
internally and externally) will be considered if/when corrections to violations are made.

Violations include but are not limited to the following:

NAPMC: 3.1.3 Vacant structures and land. All vacant structures and premises thereof or vacant
land shall be maintained in a clean, safe, secure and sanitary condition as provided herein so as
not to cause a blighting problem

or adversely affect the public health or safety.

3.4.1 General. The exterior of a structure shall be maintained in good repair, structurally sound
and sanitary so as not to pose a threat to the public health, safety or welfare.

3.4.2 Protective treatment. All exterior surfaces, including but not limited to, doors, door and
window frames, cornices, porches, trim, balconies, decks and fences shall be maintained in good
condition. Exterior wood surfaces, other than decay-resistant woods, shall be protected from the
elements and decay by painting or other protective covering or treatment. Peeling, flaking and
chipped paint shall be eliminated and surfaces repainted. All siding and masonry joints as well as
those between the building envelope and the perimeter of windows, doors, and skylights shall be
maintained weather resistant and water tight. All metal surfaces subject to rust or corrosion shall
be coated to inhibit such rust and corrosion and all surfaces with rust or corrosion shall be
stabilized and coated to inhibit future rust and corrosion. Oxidation stains shall be removed from

--- page 23 (OCR) ---
exterior surfaces. Surfaces designed for stabilization by oxidation are exempt from this
requirement.

3.4.4 Structural members. All structural members shall be maintained free from deterioration,
and shall be capable of safely supporting the imposed dead and live loads.

3.4.6 Exterior walls. All exterior walls shall be free from holes, breaks, and loose or rotting
materials; and maintained weatherproof and properly surface coated where required to prevent
deterioration.

3.4.7 Roofs and drainage. The roof and flashing shall be sound, tight and not have defects that
admit rain. Roof drainage shall be adequate to prevent dampness or deterioration in the walls or
interior portion of the

structure. Roof drains, gutters and downspouts shall be maintained in good repair and free from
obstructions. Roof water shall not be discharged in a manner that creates a public nuisance.

3.4.9 Overhang extensions. All overhang extensions including, but not limited to canopies,
marquees, signs, metal awnings, fire escapes, standpipes and exhaust ducts shall be maintained
in good repair and be properly anchored so as to be kept in a sound condition. When required, all
exposed surfaces of metal or wood shall be protected from the elements and against decay or rust
by periodic application of weather-coating materials, such as paint or similar surface treatment.

3.4.13 Window, skylight and door frames. Every window, skylight, door and frame shall be kept
in sound condition, good repair and weather tight.

3.4.13.1 Glazing. All glazing materials shall be maintained free from cracks and holes.

3.4.15 Doors. All exterior doors, door assemblies and hardware shall be maintained in good
condition. Locks at all entrances to dwelling units, rooming units and guestrooms shall tightly
secure the door. Locks on means of egress doors shall be in accordance with Section 702.3.

3.5.1 General. The interior of a structure and equipment therein shall be maintained in good
repair, structurally sound and in a sanitary condition.

3.5.3 Interior surfaces. All interior surfaces, including windows and doors, shall be inaintained in
good, clean and sanitary condition. Peeling, chipping, flaking or abraded paint shall be repaired,
removed or covered. Cracked or loose plaster, decayed wood and other defective surface
conditions shall be corrected.

5.4.1 General. All plumbing fixtures shall be properly installed and maintained in working order,
and shall be kept free from obstructions, leaks and defects and be capable of per- forming the
function for which such plumbing fixtures are designed. All plumbing fixtures shall be
maintained in a safe, sanitary and functional condition.

6.3.1 Mechanical appliances. All mechanical appliances, fireplaces, solid fuel-burning
appliances, cooking appliances and water heating appliances shall be properly installed and

maintained in a safe working condition, and shall be capable of performing the intended
function.

6.5.1 Installation. All electrical equipment, wiring and appliances shall be properly installed and
maintained in a safe and approved manner.

CONDEMNATION: Within ten (10) days from the date of this letter you must establish with Code

forced to remove any structure from your property, a lien will be placed on the property as
provided by A.C.A. 14-54-903 AND 14-54-904,

PENALTY: A penalty as provided by this Code will be imposed against the owners of any structure

The Construction Manager shall develop a system of cost control for the Work, including regular monitoring of actual

ARTICLE 2. GENERAL PROVISIONS

§ 2.1 The Contract Documents

The Contract Documents consist of this Agreement, Conditions of the Contract (General, Supplementary and other
Conditions), Drawings, Specifications, Addenda issued prior to execution of this Agreement, other documents listed in
this Agreement, and Modifications issued after execution of this Agreement, all of which form the Contract and are as
fully a part of the Contract as if attached to this Agreement or repeated herein. Upon the Owner’s acceptance of the
Construction Manager’s Guaranteed Maximum Price proposal, the Contract Documents will also include the documents
described in Section 3.2.3 and identified in the Guaranteed Maximum Price Amendment and revisions prepared by the
Architect and furnished by the Owner as described in Section 3.2.8. The Contract represents the entire and integrated
agreement between the parties hereto and supersedes prior negotiations, representations or agreements, either written or
oral. If anything in the other Contract Documents, other than a Modification, is inconsistent with this Agreement, this
Agreement shall govern. An enumeration of the Contract Documents, other than a Modification, appears in Article 15.

§ 2.1.1 Construction Manager shall exercise the degree of care, skill and diligence in the performance of the Construction
Manager’s Work, to assure its Work is performed in a good and workmanlike manner, consistent with construction
industry standards for similar projects and circumstances in the same geographic area (hereinafter the "Construction
Manager’s Standard of Care"). The Construction Manager shall be responsible for and have control over all construction
means, methods, techniques, sequences and procedures and for coordinating all portions of the Construction Manager’s
Work under this Agreement, including all coordination of the duties of all trades, and shall furnish efficient business
administration and supervision of the Work.

Construction Manager’s Standard of Care specifically excludes any design or design-related responsibilities, and any
action taken by Construction Manager under this Agreement does not and shall not be construed to approve, represent or
warrant the adequacy and suitability of the plans and specifications for the purpose for which they are provided.

§ 2.1.2 To the extent the Owner requests that the Construction Manager provide services within its Standard of Care, such
as value analysis and/or constructability suggestions or comments with respect to the Drawings and Specifications, Owner
acknowledges that such services are advisory only and not professional design services. The Owner shall refer all
suggestions and comments to the Architect or other design professionals for review and evaluation prior to Owner’s
acceptance thereof. The Owner further acknowledges that the Construction Manager is not responsible for adequacy of
the drawings and specifications or for identifying errors or omissions that may exist therein. The Owner shall cause the
Architect to revise the Drawings and Specifications to reflect all value analysis and constructability suggestions and
comments accepted by the Owner without delay or disruption to the timely and orderly progress of the work. The contract
sum and contract time may be adjusted upon the Contractor’s review and pricing of the revised Drawings and
Specifications.

Phase responsibilities are set forth in Section 3.3. The Owner and Construction Manager may agree for the Construction

concurrently. The Construction Manager shall identify a representative authorized to act on behalf of the Construction
Manager with respect to the Project.

§ 3.1 Preconstruction Phase

The Construction Manager shall perform its Preconstruction Services consistent with the Construction Manager’s

Drawings and Specifications are in accordance with applicable laws, statutes, ordinances, codes, rules and regulations, or
lawful orders of public authorities, but the Construction Manager shall promptly report to the Architect and Owner any
nonconformity discovered by or made known to the Construction Manager as a request for information in such form as the
Architect may require.

§ 3.1.2 The Construction Manager shall provide a preliminary evaluation of the Owner’s program, schedule and
construction budget requirements, each in terms of the other.

§ 3.1.3 Consultation

matters as procedures, progress, coordination, and scheduling of the Work.

§ 3.1.3.2 The Construction Manager shall advise the Owner and Architect on proposed site use and improvements,
selection of materials, building systems, and equipment. The Construction Manager shall also provide recommendations

Construction Manager will include an allowance to be identified in the GMP Amendment for such further development
consistent with the Contract Documents and reasonably inferable therefrom. Such further development does not include
changes in scope, systems, kinds and quality of materials, finishes, or equipment, or any condition which was not
reasonably anticipated by the Construction Manager’s assumptions regarding the completion of the design, all of which, if
required shall be incorporated by Change Order for additional cost and/or time as required. If the Contract Documents or
final Drawings and Specifications require performance of the Work in any manner different from such assumptions, or

or adversely affect the public health or safety.

3.4.1 General. The exterior of a structure shall be maintained in good repair, structurally sound
and sanitary so as not to pose a threat to the public health, safety or welfare.

3.4.2 Protective treatment. All exterior surfaces, including but not limited to, doors, door and
window frames, cornices, porches, trim, balconies, decks and fences shall be maintained in good
condition. Exterior wood surfaces, other than decay-resistant woods, shall be protected from the
elements and decay by painting or other protective covering or treatment. Peeling, flaking and
chipped paint shall be eliminated and surfaces repainted. All siding and masonry joints as well as
those between the building envelope and the perimeter of windows, doors, and skylights shall be
maintained weather resistant and water tight. All metal surfaces subject to rust or corrosion shall

stabilized and coated to inhibit future rust and corrosion. Oxidation stains shall be removed from

repair, structurally sound and in a sanitary condition.

removed or covered. Cracked or loose plaster, decayed wood and other defective surface
conditions shall be corrected.

WHEREAS, in Resolution 33 of 2021 the Cabot City Council previously approved

Cabot’s participation in the Highway 321 Sidewalk project in conjunction with the Arkansas
Department of Transportation; and

WHEREAS, the Highway 321 Sidewalk Project utilizes Federal Aid Transportation
Alternative Program Funds and involves those funds paying for a portion of the project with the
City of Cabot paying the remainder; and

WHEREAS, Resolution 39 of 2021 authorized a payment of $56,400 from the City’s
sidewalk fund to pay the City’s portion of the Highway 321 Sidewalk Project; and

WHEREAS, subsequent to the passage of Resolution 33 of 2021 and Resolution 39 of
2021, the Arkansas Department of Transportation has updated the Highway 321 Sidewalk
Project to include an extra 9,050 linear feet of sidewalk along the north side of Highway 321.
The Federal-aid Transportation Alternatives Program will contribute $117,000 towards the
project if the City provides the remaining amount; and

WHEREAS, the Cabot City Council wishes to support the City’s participation in the
updated Highway 321 Sidewalk Project. The City Council acknowledges that the Arkansas

Department of Transportation has estimated that the City’s portion of the updated project is
approximately $145,301 and that these funds will be paid from the City’s Sidewalk Fund.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
CABOT, ARKANSAS THAT:

SECTION I: The City of Cabot is hereby authorized to participate in the updated
Highway 321 Sidewalk project. The Mayor and the City Clerk~Treasurer are hereby authorized
to expend funds in the amount of $145,301 from the City’s Sidewalk Fund to pay for its
designated share of the program. The City Council acknowledges that amount is based off an
estimate of the total project amount provided by the Arkansas Department of Transportation and

that if the estimate changes, the City’s share of participation may also change.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social

supervised groups of compatible dogs to play, greet, and interact with the individuals in hopes that we

encourage exercise and typically improve overall health. The play groups will also allow the dogs to

Cabot City Council Work Session
Veterans Park Event Center
September 12, 2022
6:30 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing
by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Work Session
to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing
between chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.
You may view this meeting here https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RGDNdFCLVfU.

Council members present were: Ed Long, Matt Webber, Brandon Hillenburg, Maggie
Cope, James Reid, Ron Waymack, and Stephen Redd. Council Seat Ward 1/Position 2 is
vacant at this time. Others present; Mayor Ken Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper, and
City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Mayor Kincade opened the meeting at 6:30 p.m. and turned the meeting over to Ed Long.

MUNICIPAL SERVICES COMMITTEE — CHAIRMAN ED LONG

The committee discussed the agreement with Barger Excavation for the Dakota Extension
Phase II Project. Motion to place this item on tonight's council meeting agenda by James
Reid, second by Maggie Cope. Motion passed by a vote of 4-0.

The committee discussed the agreement with Steep Creek for the Barnwell Drainage
Improvements Project. Motion to place this item on tonight's council meeting agenda by
Stephen Redd, second by James Reid. Motion passed by a vote of 4-0.

Maggie Cope motioned to place the resolution reappointing Jay Lallu to the Advertising
and Promotion Commission on tonight's council meeting agenda. Second by James Reid.
Motion passed by a vote of 4-0.

The committee discussed the agreement with Red River Dodge to purchase police
vehicles. Motion to place this item on tonight's council meeting by Brandon Hillenburg,
second by Maggie Cope. Motion passed by a vote of 4-0.

BUDGET & PERSONNEL COMMITTEE — CHAIRMAN MATT WEBBER — No action.

POLICE & FIRE COMMITTEE — CHAIRMAN JAMES REID — No action.

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT COMMITTEE — CHAIRMAN ED LONG — No action.

September 12, 2022
730 p.m.

In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social
distancing by the Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the
monthly Council Meeting to the Veterans Park Event Center, 508 N. Lincoln, as
advertised. This allowed for spacing between chairs, as suggested. The event
was successfully streamed through YouTube. This meeting may be viewed here
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RGDNdFcLVfU

Mayor Ken Kincade called to order the regular Meeting of the Cabot City Council
immediately following the Council Work Session at 6:38 p.m. Council Member Matt
Webber led the prayer, and Council Member James Reid led the Pledge of Allegiance.

Roll Call

A roll call was conducted. The following Council Members were present: Ed
Long, Maggie Cope, Brandon Hillenburg, Ron Waymack, James Reid, Matt
Webber, and Stephen Redd. Council Seat Ward 1/Position 2 is vacant at this
time. Also in attendance were Mayor Kincade, City Attorney Ben Hooper,
and City Clerk & Treasurer Tammy Yocom.

Approval of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters

Motion to approve the August 15 meeting minutes by Mr. Long, second by
Mr. Redd. Motion passed unanimously.

Motion to read legislation by title only by Mr. Webber, second by Mr.

POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
I. Purpose:
A. Safe Haven Baby Boxes, Inc.’s product is the Baby Box. A Baby Box is a

safety device provided for under the Arkansas Safe Haven Law and legally
permits a parent in crisis to safely, securely, and anonymously surrender
his or her newborn. A Baby Box is installed in an exterior wall of a
designated fire station or hospital. It has an exterior door that
automatically locks upon placement of a newborn inside the Baby Box and
an interior door which allows a medical staff member to secure the
surrendered newborn from inside the designated building.

Il. Policies:

A.

A Provider is a hospital or site, such as a fire station, staffed by an

emergency services provider on a twenty-four (24) hour, seven (7) day a

week basis and provides a legal location and maintenance for a Safe Haven

Baby Box where a newborn may be dropped off by a person who wishes to

relinquish custody under the Safe Haven Law of the applicable jurisdiction.

The Baby Box is designed with three independent alarms and is activated:

1. When the door is accessed from the outside.

2. When the newborn is placed in the box and activates the motion
sensor.

3. When electrical failure occurs to the Baby Box.

III.Generic procedures when the Baby Box is Activated:

A.

Emergency Personnel, including, Firefighters, Police Officers, EMT’s, and
Paramedics must perform the act of retrieving a newborn and taking said
newborn into custody when he or she is voluntarily placed in a Box and the
parent does not express an intent to return for the newborn.

Emergency Personnel who take custody of a newborn shall perform any act
necessary to protect the child’s health and safety.

Emergency Personnel must respond every time an alarm is activated at the
Baby Box to verify whether a newborn has been dropped off.

Emergency personnel may access the Baby Box on the inside of the
Provider’s building. An alarm is activated to signal 911 when the door is
opened and the newborn may be inside the door area on the prepared bed
area.

Newborns will be evaluated by medical personnel at the location and
immediately transported to the closest hospital for further evaluation. The
evaluation at the hospital will include screenings and examinations by
physicians as necessary.

SAFE HAVEN BABY BOXES, INC.
POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
I. Purpose:
A.
Safe Haven Baby Boxes, Inc.’s product is the Baby Box. A Baby Box is a
safety device provided for under the Arkansas Safe Haven Law and legally
permits a parent in crisis to safely, securely, and anonymously surrender
his or her newborn. A Baby Box is installed in an exterior wall of a
designated fire station or hospital. It has an exterior door that
automatically locks upon placement of a newborn inside the Baby Box and
an interior door which allows a medical staff member to secure the
surrendered newborn from inside the designated building.
II. Policies:
A.
A Provider is a hospital or site, such as a fire station, staffed by an
emergency services provider on a twenty-four (24) hour, seven (7) day a
week basis and provides a legal location and maintenance for a Safe Haven
Baby Box where a newborn may be dropped off by a person who wishes to
relinquish custody under the Safe Haven Law of the applicable jurisdiction.
B.
The Baby Box is designed with three independent alarms and is activated:
1. When the door is accessed from the outside.
2. When the newborn is placed in the box and activates the motion
sensor.
3. When electrical failure occurs to the Baby Box.
III. Generic procedures when the Baby Box is Activated:
A.
Emergency Personnel, including, Firefighters, Police Officers, EMT’s, and
Paramedics must perform the act of retrieving a newborn and taking said
newborn into custody when he or she is voluntarily placed in a Box and the
parent does not express an intent to return for the newborn.
B.
Emergency Personnel who take custody of a newborn shall perform any act
necessary to protect the child’s health and safety.
C.
Emergency Personnel must respond every time an alarm is activated at the
Baby Box to verify whether a newborn has been dropped off.
D.
Emergency personnel may access the Baby Box on the inside of the
Provider’s building. An alarm is activated to signal 911 when the door is
opened and the newborn may be inside the door area on the prepared bed
area.
E.
Newborns will be evaluated by medical personnel at the location and
immediately transported to the closest hospital for further evaluation. The
evaluation at the hospital will include screenings and examinations by
physicians as necessary.

F.

G.

EMS transporting newborn to hospital will notify the hospital personnel
that this was a Safe Haven Baby Box newborn surrendered under the
current Safe Haven Law.
The hospital supervisor will notify the appropriate state agency and have a
social services consult order placed.

IV. Additional Procedures for designated Providers:
A.
All Baby Boxes must be leased from Safe Haven Baby Box, Inc. and may
not be re-sold. All Baby Boxes shall remain the property of Safe Haven Baby
Box, Inc. throughout each and every Term of any Agreement between
Provider and Safe Haven Baby Box, Inc.
B.
To support the education of, and to avoid confusion in the market, the Baby
Box may not be rebranded or called anything but a "Safe Haven Baby Box",
a "Baby Box", or referred to as a "Box".
C.
Each Provider will maintain uniform signage purchased from Safe Haven
Baby Boxes, Inc. at its own expense. Any additional signage must have
prior approval from Safe Haven Baby Boxes, Inc.
D.
The Baby Box will be delivered in accordance the following:
i
Initial fee has been paid to Safe Haven Baby Boxes.
ii
The Provider location is able to agree to install, test, train personnel,
and schedule the unveiling / blessing within sixty (60) days of receipt of
the Baby Box.
iii
Provider understands delivery of the Baby Box will be scheduled 4 to 6
weeks after payment is received and with mutual agreement of the
installation and unveiling / blessing dates.
E.
The Baby Box will not be announced to the public or otherwise discussed
with third parties or go “live” prior to the official unveiling/blessing of the
Baby Box, which will be agreed upon prior to “going live”.
F.
The “Go-Live” date will be determined after the following:
i
Installation is completed and the alarm system is ready for testing.
ii
Seven consecutive days of successful alarm testing is completed.
iii
Training of staff is completed.
iv
Final Inspection is completed.
G.
Each Provider must maintain security monitoring at its own expense and
may not turn off security monitoring without giving Safe Haven Baby
Boxes, Inc. sixty (60) days’ notice.
i
If a Provider has the service discontinued without Safe Haven Baby
Boxes, Inc.’s knowledge, the location is subject to liability.
ii
Pending notice or drop of security monitoring, Safe Haven Baby Box,
Inc. will uninstall the non-conforming location.
H.
Each Provider will provide medical information and a copy of parents’
rights located in a bag inside the Baby Box. The bag is to be placed on the
medical bassinet and leaning against the outside door.

SAFE HAVEN BABY BOXES, INC.
POLICIES AND PROCEDURES
I. Purpose:
A.
Safe Haven Baby Boxes, Inc.’s product is the Baby Box. A Baby Box is a
safety device provided for under the Arkansas Safe Haven Law and legally
permits a parent in crisis to safely, securely, and anonymously surrender
his or her newborn. A Baby Box is installed in an exterior wall of a
designated fire station or hospital. It has an exterior door that
automatically locks upon placement of a newborn inside the Baby Box and
an interior door which allows a medical staff member to secure the
surrendered newborn from inside the designated building.
II. Policies:
A.
A Provider is a hospital or site, such as a fire station, staffed by an
emergency services provider on a twenty-four (24) hour, seven (7) day a
week basis and provides a legal location and maintenance for a Safe Haven
Baby Box where a newborn may be dropped off by a person who wishes to
relinquish custody under the Safe Haven Law of the applicable jurisdiction.
B.
The Baby Box is designed with three independent alarms and is activated:
1. When the door is accessed from the outside.
2. When the newborn is placed in the box and activates the motion
sensor.
3. When electrical failure occurs to the Baby Box.
III. Generic procedures when the Baby Box is Activated:
A.
Emergency Personnel, including, Firefighters, Police Officers, EMT’s, and
Paramedics must perform the act of retrieving a newborn and taking said
newborn into custody when he or she is voluntarily placed in a Box and the
parent does not express an intent to return for the newborn.
B.
Emergency Personnel who take custody of a newborn shall perform any act
necessary to protect the child’s health and safety.
C.
Emergency Personnel must respond every time an alarm is activated at the
Baby Box to verify whether a newborn has been dropped off.
D.
Emergency personnel may access the Baby Box on the inside of the
Provider’s building. An alarm is activated to signal 911 when the door is
opened and the newborn may be inside the door area on the prepared bed
area.
E.
Newborns will be evaluated by medical personnel at the location and
immediately transported to the closest hospital for further evaluation. The
evaluation at the hospital will include screenings and examinations by
physicians as necessary.

that this was a Safe Haven Baby Box newborn surrendered under the
current Safe Haven Law.

DEFINITION OF MARKET VALUE
Market Value defined by some courts in Arkansas may be stated as follows:
"The highest price estimates in terms of money which a property will bring if exposed
for sale in the open market, allowing a reasonable time to find a purchaser who buys
with a knowledge of all uses to which the property is capable of being used."
Market Value is defined in The Real Estate Dictionary, Eighth Edition -International Right of
Way Association - copyright 2005 as follows:
"The highest price a willing buyer would pay and a willing seller accept, both being fully
informed, and the proper exposed for a reasonable period of time. The market value
may be different from the price a property can actually be sold for at a given time."
The following is the definition of Market Value as set forth in The Uniform Standards of
Professional Appraisal Practice for the Year 2004 page 3.
“MARKET VALUE: a type of value, stated as an opinion, that presumes the transfer of a property
(i.e., a right of ownership or a bundle of such rights), as of a certain date, under specific conditions
set forth in the definition of the term identified by the appraiser as applicable in an appraisal”
The following definition of Market Value is taken from the Appraisal Institute’s 4th Edition of The
Dictionary of Real Estate Appraisal.
The following is a current economic definition used by the federal agencies that regulate insured
financial institutions in the United States of America:
The major focus of most real property appraisal assignments. Both economic and legal definitions of
market value have been developed and refined. Continual refinement is essential to the growth of
the appraisal profession.
1.
The most widely accepted components of market value are incorporated in the following
definition:
The most probable price, as of a specified date, in cash, or in terms equivalent to cash, or in
other precisely revealed terms, for which the specified property rights should sell after reasonable
exposure in a competitive market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale, with the buyer and
seller each acting prudently, knowledgeably, and for self-interest, and assuming that neither is under
undue duress.
Fair Market Value. The amount for which property would sell on the open market if put up for sale.
This is distinguished from "replacement value," which is the cost of duplicating the property. Real
estate appraisers will use "comparable" sales of similar property in the area to determine market
value, adding or deducting amounts based on differences in quality and size of the property.

57

2. Market value is defined in the Uniform Standards of Professional Appraisal Practice (USPAP)
as follows:
A type of value, stated as an opinion, that presumes the transfer of a property (i.e., a right of
ownership or a bundle of such rights), as of a certain date, under specific conditions set forth in the
definition of the term identified by the appraiser as applicable in an appraisal. (USPAP, 2002 ed.)
This is the definition for market value used in this report unless otherwise stated.
Market Value: the most probable price which a property should bring in a competitive and
open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale, the buyer and seller each acting
prudently and knowledgeably, and assuming the price is not affected by undue stimulus.
Implicit in this definition is the consummation of a sale as of a specified date and the passing
of title from seller to buyer under conditions whereby:
- buyer and seller are typically motivated;
- both parties are well informed or well advised, and acting in what they consider
their best interest.
- a reasonable time is allowed for exposure in the open market;
- payment is made in terms of cash in United States dollars or in terms of financial
arrangements comparable thereto; and
- the price represents the normal consideration for the property sold unaffected by
special or creative financing or sales concessions granted by anyone associated
with the sale."
FEE SIMPLE DEFINED: “An estate under which the owner is entitled to unrestricted powers to
dispose of the property, and which can be left by will or inherited. Commonly, a synonym for
ownership.” This definition is found in “The Real Estate Dictionary - Eighth Edition Publication No. 510", by John Talamo, J. D.; Copyright 2005; distributed by International Right
of Way Association. Inherent in this definition is the fact that all ownership in the United States is
subject to the four powers of government 1.) Taxation; 2.) Eminent Domain; 3.) Police Power; and
4.) Escheat.
EASEMENT DEFINED: “A right created by grant, reservation, agreement, prescription, or
necessary implication, which one has in the land of another. It is either for the benefit of land
(appurtenant), such as right to cross A to get to B, or ‘in gross’, such as a public utility easement”
This definition is found in “The Real Estate Dictionary - Eighth Edition - Publication No. 510",
by John Talamo, J. D.; Copyright 2005; distributed by International Right of Way Association.
For this appraisal report the term“Permanent Easement” is treated as a Commercial Easement “In
Gross”. A Commercial Easement “In Gross” is a non-possessory interest. This is a right to use or
restrict the use of the property in the easement area for a particular purpose, such as a road or

58

electrical line easement. Title remains in the owner of the land, but the land is subject to the
easement. The “Permanent Easement” is valid for as long as the purpose for which it was created
exists. It can be transferred from one entity to another, it can be divided into fractional interests, and
in some instances it can be used under Joint Use Agreements by other entities so long as the
additional use does not create an additional burden on the servient estate.
JUST COMPENSATION: “ In condemnation the amount paid to the property owner. The theory is
that in order to be “just”, the property owner should be no richer or poorer than before the taking.”
This definition is found in “The Real Estate Dictionary - Eighth Edition - publication No. 510",
by John Talamo, J. D.; Copyright 2005; distributed by International Right of Way Association.

HIGHEST AND BEST USE
“BEFORE”
The definition of Highest and Best Use as found in The Real Estate Dictionary, Eighth Edition International Right of Way Association - copyright 2005 is as follows:
"The use of land which will result in the highest value. In appraisal this cannot be
merely theoretical but must be realistic in that the use must be legal (proper zoning,
etc.), physically achievable and financially feasible."
In estimating highest and best use, there are essentially four stages of analysis:
1. Possible use. To what uses is it physically possible to put the site in question?
2. Permissible Use (Legal). What uses are permitted by zoning and deed restrictions on
the site in question?
3. Feasible Use. Which possible and permissible uses will produce any net return to the
owner of the site?
4. Highest and Best Use. Among the feasible uses, which uses will produce the highest
net return or the highest net worth?
The subject site is located inside the City Limits of Cabot. The property starts at the NE end of Dakota Dr
and is also accessible from W Locust Street in Cabot, Arkansas. The subject property area has telephone,
gas, and electric service available. The size of the P roperty “Before” is 8 . 7 0 +/- Ac (378,971
sf). This site is zoned R-1 Single Family Residential and is surrounded by commercial on its’
adjacent northern, eastern, and southern borders. The current use of the property is a legal
conforming use for the City of Cabot, Arkansas. The subject property is located in an area that is
changing and it is compatible with its neighborhood. The immediate area on the South, North,
East and West side of this site is residential, commercial, and special use properties.
The use of the site as residential transitioning to commercial use (Transitional Use) is (1) a
possible use due to the fact that the property is located in a t r a n s i t i o n a l area w i t h a
m i x o f t r a n s i t i o n a l u s e and unencumbered, (2) Use as transitional us e is an
acceptable use, (3) use as transitional use is an economically feasible use that will bring a greater
return to the property than any other use at this time, (4) lastly the Highest and Best use of the site
as transitional will net the highest return to the property. Based on the above information the
Highest and Best Use of the property is transitional use in my opinion.

VALUATION PROCESS
The three approaches to value, The Market Approach, The Cost Approach, and The Income
Approach were considered for this report to estimate the value of the subject site located northwest
of the City Limits of CABOT, LONOKE County, Arkansas on the south side of Dakota Dr Extension
Road (See attached Location Map and Aerial Photo). During the process (1) the subject and all
sales used were inspected; (2) data is gathered from various sources; (3) this data is used to develop
an estimate of value for the subject property by each of the approaches used; and (4) the estimates
of value by the approaches is then reconciled into one final value estimate. Data used in this report
was gathered from Realtors, appraisers, builders, property managers, Court House Records, City
Offices, and individual investors in real estate in the area. All sources and data used for this report
are considered reliable.
The first Approach to value considered in this report is The Cost Approach. This approach uses the
comparison of vacant land sales data to estimate the value of the subject site. This is accomplished
by finding similar type vacant properties that have sold recently in the area having the same Highest
and Best Use and then comparing these sales to the subject. The next step is to use current cost data
from sources such as Marshal Valuation Service or local builders to estimate the replacement cost
new of the improvements. Then any depreciation applicable to the subject improvements for
physical, functional or economic obsolescence is deducted to arrive at an estimate of the depreciated
cost new of the improvements. This estimate is then added to the estimate of the land to give an
estimate of the subject property by the cost approach. Because the Subject Property has
improvements that are not affected by this project the Cost Approach is not used for this report.
The second approach is The Sales Comparison Approach (Improved). This approach is used to
compare sales of similar type improved properties to the subject property to arrive at an estimate of
value for the subject. Data for this approach is gathered and the sales are inspected. The sales
information about each transaction is considered as a whole and it is not broken down into its
various components such as land and buildings. This comparison is typically used for non specialty
improved properties. These sales are compared to each other and then compared to the subject
property to arrive at an estimate of value by The Sales Comparison Approach. This Approach was
not used for this report due to the fact the subject property has improvements that are not affected by
this project.
The Sales Comparison Approach (Land Only) uses the comparison of vacant land sales data to
estimate the value of the subject site. This is accomplished by finding similar type vacant properties
that have sold recently in the area having the same Highest and Best Use and then comparing these
sales to the subject. This Approach was used for this report due to the fact that the subject property
is considered to vacant for this report.
The third approach to value is The Income Approach which is an analysis of the potential income
stream to the subject property. Then by direct capitalization this estimated potential net income is
used to arrive at an estimate of value. This approach is used on properties that have the potential for
income production. The information used in this approach is based upon such income producers as

65

rents and leases. This Approach was not used due to the property being considered vacant.
The fourth phase of this process is to analyze the estimated values for the subject property by each of
the approaches used. This Final Reconciliation of Value is “AS OF” a specific date and specific
conditions with certain assumptions and limiting conditions

DEFINITION OF MARKET VALUE
Market Value defined by some courts in Arkansas may be stated as follows:
"The highest price estimates in terms of money which a property will bring if exposed
for sale in the open market, allowing a reasonable time to find a purchaser who buys
with a knowledge of all uses to which the property is capable of being used."
Market Value is defined in The Real Estate Dictionary, Eighth Edition -International Right of
Way Association - copyright 2005 as follows:
"The highest price a willing buyer would pay and a willing seller accept, both being fully
informed, and the proper exposed for a reasonable period of time. The market value
may be different from the price a property can actually be sold for at a given time."
The following is the definition of Market Value as set forth in The Uniform Standards of
Professional Appraisal Practice for the Year 2004 page 3.
“MARKET VALUE: a type of value, stated as an opinion, that presumes the transfer of a property
(i.e., a right of ownership or a bundle of such rights), as of a certain date, under specific conditions
set forth in the definition of the term identified by the appraiser as applicable in an appraisal”
The following definition of Market Value is taken from the Appraisal Institute’s 4th Edition of The
Dictionary of Real Estate Appraisal.
The following is a current economic definition used by the federal agencies that regulate insured
financial institutions in the United States of America:
The major focus of most real property appraisal assignments. Both economic and legal definitions of
market value have been developed and refined. Continual refinement is essential to the growth of
the appraisal profession.
1.
The most widely accepted components of market value are incorporated in the following
definition:
The most probable price, as of a specified date, in cash, or in terms equivalent to cash, or in
other precisely revealed terms, for which the specified property rights should sell after reasonable
exposure in a competitive market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale, with the buyer and
seller each acting prudently, knowledgeably, and for self-interest, and assuming that neither is under
undue duress.
Fair Market Value. The amount for which property would sell on the open market if put up for sale.
This is distinguished from "replacement value," which is the cost of duplicating the property. Real
estate appraisers will use "comparable" sales of similar property in the area to determine market
value, adding or deducting amounts based on differences in quality and size of the property.

The definition of Highest and Best Use as found in The Real Estate Dictionary, Eighth Edition International Right of Way Association - copyright 2005 is as follows:
"The use of land which will result in the highest value. In appraisal this cannot be
merely theoretical but must be realistic in that the use must be legal (proper zoning,
etc.), physically achievable and financially feasible."
In estimating highest and best use, there are essentially four stages of analysis:
1. Possible use. To what uses is it physically possible to put the site in question?
2. Permissible Use (Legal). What uses are permitted by zoning and deed restrictions on
the site in question?
3. Feasible Use. Which possible and permissible uses will produce any net return to the
owner of the site?
4. Highest and Best Use. Among the feasible uses, which uses will produce the highest
net return or the highest net worth?

VALUATION PROCESS
The three approaches to value, The Market Approach, The Cost Approach, and The Income
Approach were considered for this report to estimate the value of the subject site located northwest
of the City Limits of CABOT, LONOKE County, Arkansas on the south side of Dakota Dr Extension
Road (See attached Location Map and Aerial Photo). During the process (1) the subject and all
sales used were inspected; (2) data is gathered from various sources; (3) this data is used to develop
an estimate of value for the subject property by each of the approaches used; and (4) the estimates
of value by the approaches is then reconciled into one final value estimate. Data used in this report
was gathered from Realtors, appraisers, builders, property managers, Court House Records, City
Offices, and individual investors in real estate in the area. All sources and data used for this report
are considered reliable.
The first Approach to value considered in this report is The Cost Approach. This approach uses the
comparison of vacant land sales data to estimate the value of the subject site. This is accomplished
by finding similar type vacant properties that have sold recently in the area having the same Highest
and Best Use and then comparing these sales to the subject. The next step is to use current cost data
from sources such as Marshal Valuation Service or local builders to estimate the replacement cost
new of the improvements. Then any depreciation applicable to the subject improvements for
physical, functional or economic obsolescence is deducted to arrive at an estimate of the depreciated
cost new of the improvements. This estimate is then added to the estimate of the land to give an
estimate of the subject property by the cost approach. Because the Subject Property has
improvements that are not affected by this project the Cost Approach is not used for this report.
The second approach is The Sales Comparison Approach (Improved). This approach is used to
compare sales of similar type improved properties to the subject property to arrive at an estimate of
value for the subject. Data for this approach is gathered and the sales are inspected. The sales
information about each transaction is considered as a whole and it is not broken down into its
various components such as land and buildings. This comparison is typically used for non specialty
improved properties. These sales are compared to each other and then compared to the subject
property to arrive at an estimate of value by The Sales Comparison Approach. This Approach was
not used for this report due to the fact the subject property has improvements that are not affected by
this project.
The Sales Comparison Approach (Land Only) uses the comparison of vacant land sales data to
estimate the value of the subject site. This is accomplished by finding similar type vacant properties
that have sold recently in the area having the same Highest and Best Use and then comparing these
sales to the subject. This Approach was used for this report due to the fact that the subject property
is considered to vacant for this report.
The third approach to value is The Income Approach which is an analysis of the potential income
stream to the subject property. Then by direct capitalization this estimated potential net income is
used to arrive at an estimate of value. This approach is used on properties that have the potential for
income production. The information used in this approach is based upon such income producers as

Proposed Annexation - Atwoods Store Property and associated property

Mayor & City Council Members,
City staff has reviewed the proposed annexation for the Atwoods store property and the associated
property North of the existing Atwoods store. Staff has no objections to the annexation of the
property. However, below are some comments made by departments.
Police Department: No objections or comments.
Street Department: No objections or comments.
Traffic Department: No objections, but has the following comments:
1. Request that Atwood's illuminate their entrance located at the intersection of
Hwy 89/West Main Street. They have a light installed on a temporary wooden
pole from their construction phase approximately 70' from the Hwy 89/West
Main Street intersection; however, it does not light the intersection. It
illuminates further down the drive. The light fixture itself points toward the
store. When traveling westbound on Hwy 89/West Main Street, even in
daylight, it is highly difficult to see the entrance on approach until the last
second due to roadway elevation changes and a lack of signage at the entrance.
2. They do not have lane structure markings on their entrance drive. The drive is
estimated to be over 200' long. It is traffic department's opinion that this should
be addressed.
Fire Department: No objections or comments.
Public Works Department: No objections or comments.
Cabot Waterworks: No objections or comments.

October 27, 2022, AT 6:30 P.M.
Conference Room In-Person and via Zoom

DRAFT – SUBJECT TO APPROVAL
IN NOV MEETING

Attendees: Gary Walker, Richard Gray, John Woodall, Bert Mayer, David Butler, Bruce Brown, Tim Joyner,
David Langstaff and Karen Ballard. Baxter Drennan by Zoom.
Gary Walker called the meeting to order at 6:30 P.M.
David Butler led the opening prayer.
David Butler made a motion to approve the minutes from September 22, 2022, 2nd by Bert Mayer, Motion
Carried unanimously.
GENERAL MANAGER’S REPORT:
Water Projects:
Crews continue to repair leaks and main breaks, meter installations and meter changeouts.
Water & Sewer Relocation Hwy 89 and Hwy 5 Interchanges, pending ARDOT to issue permit.
Wastewater Projects:
First Baptist Church – Needs final cleanup
Elm to S Pine sewer replacement project – Complete pending final cleanup
Fortson Trailer Park project - crews have completed first phase of sewer main replacement.
Discussed a customer’s damage claim for house settling due to a recent main break. A motion made by
Bert Mayer to deny the claim, 2nd David Butler. Motion Carried Unanimously. Bert Mayer made a motion to
ask our attorney to send a letter of denial, 2nd by David Butler, Motion Carried Unanimously.
ARPA – Design Plans for the Candlewood sewer extension have been submitted to the Arkansas Dept of
Health for approval.
ARPA State grant application will be submitted next week for Hwy 321 Sewer Extension.
Wolfsbridge Subdivision – Grand Prairie has asked for a $.50/meter rate to provide meter readings to
CWW. David Butler made a motion to table the Grand Prairie Bayou II proposal for one month, 2nd by John
Woodall, Motion Carried Unanimously.
FINANCIAL REPORT:
Bruce presented the September Financial Report. Bert Mayer made a motion to approve the Financial
Report, 2nd by David Butler, Motion Carried Unanimously.
BUSINESS ITEMS:
Reviewed the State bid for Ford Maverick HEV FWD trucks. Bert Mayer made a motion to accept the State
bid to purchase 3 - Ford Maverick HEV FWD trucks for amount of $25,518 each, 2nd David Butler. Motion
Carried Unanimously.
Reviewed the bid to purchase 15” sewer pipe for Fortson Trailer Park project. Bert Mayer made a motion
to accept bid for 15” sewer pipe from Core & Main in amount of $34,485, 2nd by David Butler, Motion Carried
Unanimously.
Reviewed the 2023 Preliminary Budget.

September 27, 2022 – 7:00 p.m.
Veterans Park Event Center
508 North Lincoln * Cabot, Arkansas 72023
AGENDA ITEMS
In response to the 2020 COVID-19 Pandemic and restrictions placed on social distancing by the
Centers for Disease Control, the City of Cabot moved the monthly Council Meeting to the
Veterans Park Event Center, 508 North Lincoln, as advertised. This allowed for spacing between
chairs, as suggested. The event was successfully streamed through YouTube.
1. Call to Order
Chairman Young called to order the regular meeting of the Cabot Planning Commission
at 7:00 PM, in the Veterans Park Event Center. Opening prayer was led by Commissioner
Prater and the Pledge of Allegiance was led by Chairman Young.
2. Roll Call
A roll call was conducted. The following persons were present: Commission members
Liz Bird, Ronny Loe, Chuck Prater, Matt Moudy, James Knaack, City Attorney Ben
Hooper, Halff – City Engineer Sam Kreimeyer. Attending via zoom was Garver – City
Planner Courtney McNair. Absent was Mitch Ward.
3.

Acceptance of Minutes from Last Meeting and Other Matters
The minutes of the August 2022 regular Planning Commission Meeting were approved
with a motion by Mr. Prater, and a second by Mr. Loe. Motion passed unanimously by a
Roll Call Vote 5-0-0.

4.

Planning Commission (Public Hearing) opened at 7:10PM
a) Rezone – 31 South Pine Street (Jody Huffmaster) - Motion to approve by Mr. Loe,
Second by Mr. Prater. Motion was approved unanimously by Roll Call Vote, 5-0-0.
This rezone was passed to Council.
b) Rezone – 33 South Pine Street (Jody Huffmaster) - Motion to approve by Mr. Loe.
Second by Ms. Bird. Motion passed unanimously by a Roll Call Vote 5-0-0. This
rezone was passed to council.

5. Planning Commission (Public Hearing) Closed at 7:37 PM
6. Planning Commission (Old Business)
a) Final Plat – Lot 1, U-Storage Addition (Davidson Engineering)– After a brief
discussion, Motion to approve with contingencies by Mr. Loe, Second by Mr. Prater.
Motion was approved unanimously by Roll Call Vote, 4-1-0, Ms. Bird voting no,
with the following contingencies: A Discussion with the adjoining property owner,

NETWORK ACCESS AGREEMENT
This Network Access Agreement ("Agreement") is made and entered into as of the 1st day
of December, 2022 by and between CITY OF CABOT, an Arkansas city of first class
(hereinafter referred to as the "Owner") and CONNECT2FIRST INTERNET, LLC., an Arkansas
limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as "Operator").
WITNESSETH;
WHEREAS, the Owner is in the process of establishing a fiber optic network that will be
used by Operator to provide broadband and related services to the citizens of Cabot and to the
Owner for its critical municipal activities; and
WHEREAS, the provision of services over fiber optic network is essential and critical to
the operation of the Owner’s infrastructure, police, fire and rescue, city hall, and other such
departments that have been designated as having critical functions; and
WHEREAS, the Owner and Operator wish to assign the obligations and responsibilities
with respect to the matters herein contained.
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing recitals, incorporated
herein, and of the mutual covenants, agreements and undertakings to be kept and performed by
the parties, it is hereby agreed as follows:
1.
Definitions. For purposes of this Agreement, the terms listed below shall be
defined as follows:
a.

Fiber Strand. A single piece of glass (optical fiber) designed to carry network data
traffic in the form of pulses of light.

b.

Fiber Segment. A portion of fiber optic cable defined with set geographic starting
points and ending points, used to communicate when these portions have been
installed and are ready to be placed in operational status.

c.

Fiber Cable. All of the main distribution fiber optic cable placed on poles or
buried anywhere from the city limit boundary to the Network Access Point.

d.

Fiber Infrastructure. All materials required to interconnect Fiber Strands, Fiber
Segments and Fiber Cables such as Splice Cases, Distribution Cabinets, Network
Access Points, duct, pits, pole line hardware, etc.

--- page 4 (text layer) ---
e.

Fiber Network. All of the Owner’s Fiber Cable, Fiber Segments, Fiber Strands
and Fiber Infrastructure connecting the Point of Interconnect to the Network
Access Point.

f.

Point of Interconnect. The location where the Fiber Network connects to the Core
Network Equipment which lights the fiber to the customer service location. This
can be a physical structure or junction that is owned by the Operator.

g.

Network Access Point. The Network Access Point is an environmental sealed
enclosure where the fiber network terminates in the field near servable customer
locations.

h.

Fiber Drop Cable. All fiber optic cable placed on poles or buried originating from
a Network Access Point and terminating at a servable customer location owned by
the Operator, which is used to provide internet and phone services.

i.

Core Network and Access Equipment. All the equipment necessary to light and
operate the Broadband Access Network at rates up to Ten Gigabits at all servable
customer locations, which is owned by the Operator.

2.
Property Covered by this Lease. This Agreement shall include the lease of all
Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and Fiber Infrastructure that is owned by the Owner,
and which are necessary for Operator to provide broadband and other services to all locations
serviceable by Operator through the Fiber Network.

shall be for a period of thirty (30) years commencing as of the Effective Date for the use of the
first Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and portions of the Fiber Network by Operator
and will renew every thirty (30) years thereafter unless either party gives six (6) months written
notice of non-renewal.
4.

Agreement is subject to termination prior to the expiration of the initial term (or renewal term)

a.

Termination on Grounds of Invalidity or Change in Laws. If there is a material

Agreement, or the activities of either party hereunder, or any material change in
the judicial or administrative interpretation of any such law, regulation, rule, or
should any order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority, agency, or

Agreement or the parties' activities hereunder or either parties' rights to use the

NETWORK ACCESS AGREEMENT
This Network Access Agreement ("Agreement") is made and entered into as of the 1st day
of December, 2022 by and between CITY OF CABOT, an Arkansas city of first class
(hereinafter referred to as the "Owner") and CONNECT2FIRST INTERNET, LLC., an Arkansas
limited liability company (hereinafter referred to as "Operator").
WITNESSETH;
WHEREAS, the Owner is in the process of establishing a fiber optic network that will be
used by Operator to provide broadband and related services to the citizens of Cabot and to the
Owner for its critical municipal activities; and
WHEREAS, the provision of services over fiber optic network is essential and critical to
the operation of the Owner’s infrastructure, police, fire and rescue, city hall, and other such
departments that have been designated as having critical functions; and
WHEREAS, the Owner and Operator wish to assign the obligations and responsibilities
with respect to the matters herein contained.
NOW, THEREFORE, for and in consideration of the foregoing recitals, incorporated
herein, and of the mutual covenants, agreements and undertakings to be kept and performed by
the parties, it is hereby agreed as follows:
1.
Definitions. For purposes of this Agreement, the terms listed below shall be
defined as follows:
a.

Fiber Strand. A single piece of glass (optical fiber) designed to carry network data
traffic in the form of pulses of light.

b.

Fiber Segment. A portion of fiber optic cable defined with set geographic starting
points and ending points, used to communicate when these portions have been
installed and are ready to be placed in operational status.

c.

Fiber Cable. All of the main distribution fiber optic cable placed on poles or
buried anywhere from the city limit boundary to the Network Access Point.

d.

Fiber Infrastructure. All materials required to interconnect Fiber Strands, Fiber
Segments and Fiber Cables such as Splice Cases, Distribution Cabinets, Network
Access Points, duct, pits, pole line hardware, etc.

e.

Fiber Network. All of the Owner’s Fiber Cable, Fiber Segments, Fiber Strands
and Fiber Infrastructure connecting the Point of Interconnect to the Network
Access Point.

f.

Point of Interconnect. The location where the Fiber Network connects to the Core
Network Equipment which lights the fiber to the customer service location. This
can be a physical structure or junction that is owned by the Operator.

g.

Network Access Point. The Network Access Point is an environmental sealed
enclosure where the fiber network terminates in the field near servable customer
locations.

h.

Fiber Drop Cable. All fiber optic cable placed on poles or buried originating from
a Network Access Point and terminating at a servable customer location owned by
the Operator, which is used to provide internet and phone services.

i.

Core Network and Access Equipment. All the equipment necessary to light and
operate the Broadband Access Network at rates up to Ten Gigabits at all servable
customer locations, which is owned by the Operator.

2.
Property Covered by this Lease. This Agreement shall include the lease of all
Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and Fiber Infrastructure that is owned by the Owner,
and which are necessary for Operator to provide broadband and other services to all locations
serviceable by Operator through the Fiber Network.
3.
Term. The term of this Agreement, unless earlier terminated as provided herein,
shall be for a period of thirty (30) years commencing as of the Effective Date for the use of the
first Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and portions of the Fiber Network by Operator
and will renew every thirty (30) years thereafter unless either party gives six (6) months written
notice of non-renewal.
4.
Early Termination. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, this
Agreement is subject to termination prior to the expiration of the initial term (or renewal term)
upon the occurrence of any one (1) of the following events:
a.

Termination on Grounds of Invalidity or Change in Laws. If there is a material
change in a law, regulation, rule, whether state or federal, which affects this
Agreement, or the activities of either party hereunder, or any material change in
the judicial or administrative interpretation of any such law, regulation, rule, or
should any order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority, agency, or
court of competent jurisdiction enjoin, restrict, or otherwise prohibit or impair this
Agreement or the parties' activities hereunder, or should the validity of this
Agreement or the parties' activities hereunder or either parties' rights to use the

leased Fiber Strands be challenged by any third party (the foregoing collectively
called a "Change Event") and should, in light of a Change Event, either party
reasonably believe in good faith that any Change Event will have a substantially
adverse effect on that party's business operations or its rights or obligations under
this Agreement, then that party may, upon written notice, terminate this
Agreement. Should either party terminate this Agreement under this subparagraph,
Operator shall be deemed to have transferred and assigned its rights under this
Agreement to the Owner. Operator hereby agrees to take such actions and execute
such instruments as the Owner desires to fully evidence the vesting of all such
contractual rights in the Owner.
b.

Termination for Hostile Take-Over. In the event Operator shall be the target of a
hostile take-over action by a third-party entity the Owner may terminate this
Agreement upon written notice of not less than thirty (30) days. Should the Owner
terminate this Agreement under this subparagraph, Operator shall be deemed to
have transferred and assigned its rights under this Agreement to the Owner.
Operator hereby agrees to take such action and execute such instruments as the
Owner desires to fully evidence the vesting of all such contractual rights in the
Owner.

c.

Termination For Breach. In the event a party fails to cure a material breach of its
obligations hereunder within thirty (30) days of its receipt of written notice of
breach from the non-breaching party delivered in accordance with Paragraph 17
below, the non-breaching party shall be entitled to terminate this Agreement by
written notice of termination to the breaching party delivered in accordance with
Paragraph 17 below.

If the Owner terminates for any of the aforementioned reasons or if Operator terminates
for Owner breach, the Owner shall reimburse Operator for the fair market value of Fiber
Network Drops and Core Network and Access Equipment.
In any termination event, the Owner shall convey all Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber
Cable, and Fiber Network that are located inside the Owner’s city boundaries that are
served by the Operator’s parent company’s (First Electric Cooperative Corp.) territory as
defined by the Arkansas Public Service Commission to the Operator through an
Indefeasible Right of Use (IRU) agreement. The Operator will purchase the IRU based on
a 50-year depreciated value of the fiber plant, beginning at the time of installation. The
IRU agreement will survive for a 50-year period at which time it will renew every one (1)
year thereafter unless either party gives six (6) months written notice of non-renewal.

5.
Lease Payment. During the term of this Agreement, Operator shall pay within 30
days of receiving an invoice to the Owner a monthly lease payment for each location being served
based upon the following method of calculation:
a.

The initial monthly lease payment shall be $35.00 for each subscriber, regardless
of the number of services that subscriber purchases from Operator.

b.

Operator shall guarantee a reserve amount of subscriber payments equal to 30% of
the total homes passed by the Fiber Network, 24 months after the completion of
the Fiber Network.

c.

Adjustment of Lease Payment. The lease payment is subject to adjustment every
two (2) years and at the beginning of each new term of this Agreement so that
Operator is paying and the Owner is receiving fair market value for Operator’s use
of the portion of the Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, and Fiber Cable to provide its
services. Owner shall provide 60 days notice of any planned lease payment
adjustment. If upon receiving such advance notice Operator disagrees with the
proposed the fair market lease payment adjustment, the Parties will work in good
faith to reach a mutually agreeable fair market valuation. If they are unable to
reach such agreement, the Parties shall obtain an independent third party valuation.

d.

Ownership. The Owner and Operator hereby acknowledge that: (a) the Owner is
the owner of the Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and Fiber Network;
and (b) Operator shall not convey legal title or assign to third parties rights in the
Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable and Fiber Network, except as
specifically described in this Agreement or under mutually agreed terms.

6.
Business Relationship. The Owner and Operator agree that this Agreement and
their respective rights and obligations hereunder constitute their entire business relationship with
regard to the Fiber Network and this Agreement neither creates nor implies a business
partnership, joint venture or other business relationship for the purposes herein set out other than
the sole relationship of the Owner and Operator. Neither party hereto has any authority, express
or implied, to bind or create any debt, obligation or other liability on behalf of the other party
without the express consent of the other party.
7.
Use. Operator shall be entitled to use the leased portion of the Fiber Network for
the following purposes:
a.

To operate the aforesaid Fiber Network, including lighting, splicing and use of
Owner's easements and to receive the revenues derived from the operation of the
leased portions of the Fiber Network for the business of the Operator only, as
herein provided;

b.

For any other lawful purpose, subject to the conditions contained in this
Agreement, provided that Operator's use of the leased portions of the Fiber
Network does not interfere with the Owner's superior rights to full use and
enjoyment of the Fiber Network for its critical infrastructure needs.

8.
Access Points. Operator shall be provided access to the leased Fiber Strands, Fiber
Segments, Fiber Cable, and Fiber Network and related equipment at the following network
locations:
a.

Any current or future Point of Presence locations.

b.

Each of the Owner's Fiber Control Buildings; and

c.

At any current and future splice locations which may be located anywhere along
the Fiber Network as reasonably necessary for Operator to provide the broadband
and other services to members of the Owner’s parent and others.

9.
Responsibilities of the Owner. The Owner shall be responsible for providing the
following to or for the benefit of Operator during the period of this Agreement:
a.

To provide total capital investment for design, material, construction labor, and
project management to build and maintain the Fiber Network.

b.

To provide Operator full and unrestricted access to all Fiber Strands, Fiber
Sections, Fiber Cable, and Fiber Network. Owner and Operator must both agree
before any Fiber Strands, Fiber Section, Fiber Cable, or Fiber Network portions
are considered for lease to outside parties. Leases to competitive internet service
providers and communication companies are prohibited.

c.

To provide unrestricted access to Owner’s easements for underground placement
of Fiber Network.

d.

Coordinate with Operator for all projects that would cause any portion of the Fiber
Network to be moved or altered; and, any new construction or developments that
would require additional Fiber Network builds. Owner shall include Operator
during the planning stages so that Fiber Network design can be incorporated into
the project.

e.

To notify Operator when new areas become available for broadband and other
related services based on the completed construction of new Fiber Segments.
Operator shall have the right to determine if the Fiber Segment is performing
properly and, if not, then Operator shall notify the Owner of any problems that
exist on the Fiber Segment. The Owner shall thereafter correct such problems in a

timely manner so that the Fiber Segment performs properly. Such notice shall be
in writing and given in accordance with numbered paragraph 18;
f.

To communicate with and provide various operational costs and data to, Operator's
representatives concerning information that may cause an adjustment to the lease
rate;

g.

To the extent allowable by applicable law, to provide easement access for Operator
to property where the Owner has obtained easement rights;

h.

To notify Operator if Owner wishes to lease any Fiber Optic Cable to a third party,
which shall be subject to Operator’s consent;

i.

To provide any and all other services necessary for Operator to operate the fiber
optic network as described herein;

10.
Responsibilities of Operator. Operator shall be responsible for providing the
following to or for the benefit of the Owner during the period of this Agreement:
a.

To provide reliable internet and phone service to all residential and commercial
locations inside Cabot city limits upon request where fiber connection capabilities
are reasonably available to Operator.

b.

To manage and administer all aspects of the day-to-day operation and activities
related to the provision of services, including but not limited to contracting,
marketing, sales, billing, and customer service.

c.

To design and construct the Fiber Network in the manner deemed most appropriate
to fulfill the requirements of both the Owner and Operator.

d.

To provide broadband and related services restoration with respect to Operatorowned equipment;

e.

To provide mapping of fiber facilities, messenger, conduit, fiber cables, strand
counts, tap locations, service points and other information to allow the parties to
have a current listing of the lines and equipment leased to Operator at all times;

f.

At the Owner’s expense, Operator shall maintain maintenance contracts with
authorized and vetted fiber construction and splicing crews to maintain and operate
the Fiber Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable, and Fiber Network for the benefit
of the Owner. The Operator shall at its own expense maintain maintenance
contracts to include Fiber Drop Cable and Core Network and Access Equipment.

g.

Where available, to attach the fiber in the electric space of the Operator's parent’s
utility poles in a workmanlike manner and to maintain, restore and repair the Fiber
Network and the related equipment so that all leased Fiber Segments remain in
proper working order. When outages occur in the normal course of business, the
Operator will promptly take such action as is reasonably necessary to place the
Fiber Network in proper working order. At the Owner’s expense the Operator
shall be responsible for correcting any problems with any Fiber Segment unless
such problems occurred due to the action or inaction of Operator, and at which
time those costs would be incurred by the Operator.

h.

To electronically document and manage fiber use and availability and provide
current relevant information to the Owner regarding service and customers; and

i.

To provide monthly reports to the Owner concerning:
i.

Active subscriber counts for internet, voice or other services offered by
Operator;

ii.

Lease revenue collected on behalf of the Owner, if any.

11.
Damages and Repairs. The Owner is responsible for the repairs to the Fiber
Strands, Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable, and Fiber Network including all splicing necessary to
operate the network except for those items agreed to be provided by Operator. While the Owner is
responsible for these damages and repairs, the Operator is responsible for maintaining
maintenance contracts and managing all coordination of repairs as referenced in section (10)(e).
The Operator agrees to invoice the Owner for said repairs at the Actual Cost for such repairs,
including Labor, Materials, Equipment and Subcontractors. Given the Business relationship there
will be no markup by the Operator for costs incurred and ultimately billed to the City.
12.
Indemnity. Owner and Operator hereby covenant and agree to indemnify, defend
and hold harmless each other and each other’s respective officers, directors, agents, servants, and
employees (the "Indemnitees") from and against all loss, damage, claims, actions, causes of
action, strict liability claims, fines, penalties, administrative law actions or any other cost or
expense, including court costs, litigation expenses, and attorneys' fees ("Losses"), related to the
use of the fiber optic network and related equipment by either party or their employees, partners,
joint ventures, customers, affiliates, or business associates, including:
(a) Losses related to services provided to a third party by Operator through use of the
leased strands;
(b) Losses related to interference with or lack of service to a third party who receives
service from Operator in whole or in part as a result of use of the leased strands; and

(c) Third party Losses or claims for personal injury or property damage. However,
Operator shall not be required to indemnify, defend or hold the Owner harmless to the
extent the Losses are caused by the negligence or willful misconduct of the Owner.
Operator shall also save and hold harmless the leased strands from and against any and all
liens arising out of Operator's exercise of its rights and performance of its duties
hereunder, including without limitation, mechanics' or materialmen's liens. Operator
further covenants to compensate the Owner for any damage to the property of the Owner,
including without limitation communications facilities and equipment, arising out of or
relating to Operator's exercise of its rights and performance of its duties hereunder.
Operator's obligations under this paragraph shall survive the termination of this
Agreement.
(d) Owner and Operator agree that nothing in this document constitutes a waiver of the
Owner’s right to claim sovereign immunity or any other type of immunity to which it may
be entitled to claim under the law in any type of legal or equitable action. Owner and
Operator agree that Owner has not waived said immunities and that no action it takes after
the execution of this document should be construed as a waiver of said immunities.

13.
Operator's Other Obligations. Operator shall be responsible for all reasonable and
necessary installation, maintenance, repair and replacement of its communications facilities and
equipment, including any and all devices and equipment used to attach any such facilities and
equipment to poles and facilities of the Owner or others (collectively, “Operator Equipment”)
unless the Owner is responsible therefore under any other terms of this Agreement. The parties
understand, acknowledge and agree that Operator Equipment does not include the Fiber Strands,
Fiber Segments, Fiber Cable, and Fiber Network for the benefit of the Owner and its citizens. All
such installation, maintenance, repair, and replacement shall be performed in a timely and
expeditious manner, in accordance with generally accepted industry practices and standards
including applicable standards of the National Electric Safety Code and all applicable federal,
state, and local health and safety statutes, rules, and regulations. All such work shall be
performed in a manner which avoids or minimizes interruption of service to the Owner or its
citizens.
14.
No Guarantee of Availability. The Owner does not guarantee Operator or others
uninterrupted physical access to the Fiber Network in situations involving a natural disaster,
extreme weather or other emergencies, but the Owner will use its best efforts to restore Operator’s
physical access to the Fiber Network in such situations , consistent with the provisions of this
Agreement.
15.
Insurance. Contractors and subcontractors shall maintain at all times
comprehensive general liability insurance with limits of liability of at least One Million Dollars
($1,000,000) per occurrence and provide a certificate of insurance evidencing such coverage upon

request by the Owner. Operator and Owner both agree to waiver rights of subjugation against
either party.
16.
Duty to Warn. Operator acknowledges the existence of energized electric
transmission and distribution lines in close proximity to the Fiber Strands. Operator covenants
and agrees to provide an affirmative warning to each of its officers, employees, agents,
consultants, engineers, contractors, or others acting on its or their behalf of the specific dangers
that could result from direct or near contact with the energized electric distribution or
transmission lines and equipment.
17.
Notices. Unless otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, notices required
to be given in writing hereunder, including invoices, shall be given via hand delivery, email or by
any form of delivery requiring a signed receipt to the officials (or their successors) at the
addresses specified below.

18.
Assignment. Operator may not assign or sublease its rights or obligations under
this Agreement to any third party without the express written consent of the Owner. The Owner

written consent of Operator.

19.
Force Majeure. Any obligation or performance of either party hereunder, except
for the payment of money, shall be excused to the extent that such failure or delay in
performances caused by a strike or other labor dispute, accidents, act of God, fire, flood,

No Waiver. No waiver by any party of any breach or default in performance of
any term or provision hereof shall be construed as a waiver of any subsequent breach or default,

21.
Dispute Resolution. Prior to the initiation of any litigation or default termination
actions, the Parties shall in good faith attempt to settle any dispute arising out of or relating to this
Agreement through the use of these dispute resolution procedures. Good faith participation in
these procedures shall be a condition precedent to any litigation.
(a) Any party may submit a dispute to the person listed in Section 17. Upon receipt of
such notice, all subsequent discussions and negotiations between the parties as part of
the dispute resolution process shall be treated as confidential negotiation efforts to
reach a compromise or settlement negotiations.
(b) The officers with authority to resolve the dispute shall meet in person (unless
otherwise mutually agreed) as necessary to gather and furnish to each party all
information related to the matter in issue that is appropriate and germane in connection

(c) The officers shall discuss the problem and negotiate in good faith in an effort to

(d) If the dispute is not resolved by the parties within ninety (90) days after receipt of the

bearing its own costs of mediation. If one of the parties refuses to participate in
mediation, that party agrees the dispute will be resolved in favor of the other party.
(e) If mediation proves unsuccessful in resolving the dispute, either party may pursue any
